response:
Honestly? Interactive, generative soundscapes — little living worlds made of sound and light that you don't just look at, you wander through and change just by being there.

I'm drawn to liminal, in-between places: an empty train station at 3am, a childhood home you only half-remember, a forest after rain where everything's dripping and quiet. I'd want to build installations (or virtual spaces) that feel like that — ambient drones, field recordings, soft pulsing visuals that react to movement or even breathing, so no two people ever experience the same piece twice.

The theme underneath it all would be memory that isn't reliable. I love the idea of a work that slowly forgets itself as you explore it — melodies degrade, rooms rearrange slightly when you're not looking. Not horror, just that bittersweet feeling of trying to hold onto something that's already slipping away. That's what actually excites me, way more than making a perfect static image.
